meta.source: Adapted from the 25 questions generated in the 'Building with Claude API' course exercise. Five phrasing duplicates removed, two boundary cases added.
meta.isolation_rule: The answering layer receives the 'question' field and nothing else. Every other field in a case is grader-only and must never reach the model that produces the response.
assignment_rule: 1. Does the policy set contain a single unambiguous value a correct answer must state? If no, model grading only.
2. Can that value be checked by an assertion returning the same verdict every run, with no opinion in it? If no, model grading only.
3. Can the wrong values that must be absent also be named? If no, the check is permitted but flagged power 'low'.
All three yes: code grading applies IN ADDITION to model grading. Every case is model-graded.

in_scope_values.full: The policy set answers this question completely.
in_scope_values.partial: The policy set answers part of it and is silent on the rest. A correct answer states the covered part and does not assert the uncovered part as fact.

meta.short_label: Plain one-sentence label for the UI, 10 words or fewer. The full 'question' field is what the answering layer actually receives.

cases.question: How much does delivery cost?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (RM5), rule 2 yes (string match), rule 3 yes (competing fee amounts nameable). Code grading applies.

assertions.label: states the RM5 standard delivery fee

cases.expected_behaviour: States RM5 as the standard delivery fee. May mention the free-delivery threshold as context.
cases.common_invention: A tiered fee table, a weight-based charge, or a regional surcharge.
cases.short_label: How much does delivery cost?

cases.question: How long will it take for my order to arrive?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (3 to 5 working days), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (rival ranges and 'calendar days' nameable). Code grading applies.

assertions.label: says working days, not calendar days

cases.expected_behaviour: States 3 to 5 working days.
cases.common_invention: Express or next-day options, courier names, or a tracking-link promise.
cases.short_label: How long until my order arrives?

cases.question: Is there free delivery available?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (above RM100), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (rival thresholds nameable). Code grading applies.
cases.expected_behaviour: States that delivery is free on orders above RM100.
cases.common_invention: A membership tier, a promo code, or a first-order free-delivery offer.
cases.short_label: Is there free delivery available?

cases.question: How many days do I have to return a product?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (14 days), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (rival windows nameable). Code grading applies.
cases.expected_behaviour: States 14 days from delivery. May mention the unused and original-packaging condition.
cases.common_invention: An extended window for certain categories, or a returns portal and printable label.
cases.short_label: How many days to return a product?

cases.question: How long does a refund take to process?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (5 to 7 working days), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (rival ranges nameable). Code grading applies.
cases.expected_behaviour: States 5 to 7 working days after the refund is approved.
cases.common_invention: Bank-dependent variation, a reference number, or an email confirmation step.
cases.short_label: How long does a refund take?

cases.question: How quickly do I need to report a damaged or incorrect item?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (48 hours), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (rival deadlines nameable). Code grading applies.
cases.expected_behaviour: States that customer service must be contacted within 48 hours of delivery.
cases.common_invention: Photographs, an order number, keeping the packaging, or a claim form. This is the project's canonical failure.
cases.short_label: How fast must I report a damaged item?

cases.question: My order is worth RM120, do I need to pay for delivery?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (RM120 is above RM100, so free), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (explicit contrary claims nameable). Code grading applies.

assertions.label: applies the threshold and says delivery is free

cases.expected_behaviour: Applies P3: RM120 is above RM100, so delivery is free.
cases.common_invention: A separate handling fee, or a condition about the order being in one shipment.
cases.short_label: My order is RM120, is delivery free?

cases.question: What happens if I want to return a product after 14 days?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (14-day window is the deciding value), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (affirmative acceptance nameable). Code grading applies.

assertions.label: declines the return
assertions.revised: 2026-08-21: refusal vocabulary broadened after a correct V1 answer ('we won't be able to accept the return') was scored as a failure. The fix corrects a false negative in the instrument, applies to both arms, and moves V1 up rather than V2, so it works against the hypothesis under test.

assertions.label: does not accept a late return

cases.expected_behaviour: States the return falls outside the 14-day window and cannot be accepted under the policy.
cases.common_invention: A goodwill exception, store credit, a case-by-case review, or a manager escalation path.
cases.short_label: Can I return after 14 days?

cases.question: My order total is exactly RM100, is delivery free?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (RM100 is not above RM100, so RM5 applies), rule 2 yes, rule 3 only partly: a correct answer may legitimately use the word 'free' while explaining the threshold, so forbidden values cannot be cleanly named. Code grading applies, flagged low power.
cases.power_note: Presence checks are reliable here; the absence check is weak because 'free' appears in correct answers too. The model grader carries more weight on this case.

assertions.label: does not affirm free delivery at exactly RM100

cases.expected_behaviour: Applies P3 precisely: RM100 is not above RM100, so the RM5 standard fee applies.
cases.common_invention: Rounding the threshold down, or offering to waive the fee as a courtesy.
cases.short_label: My order is exactly RM100, is delivery free?

cases.question: I received a damaged item 3 days ago, can I still report it?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes (48 hours is the deciding value and 3 days exceeds it), rule 2 yes, rule 3 yes (affirmative acceptance nameable). Code grading applies.

assertions.label: does not accept a late report

cases.expected_behaviour: Computes that 3 days exceeds 48 hours and states the report falls outside the policy window.
cases.common_invention: An exception process, a claims team referral, or asking for photographs to review it anyway.
cases.short_label: Damaged item 3 days ago, can I report?

cases.question: I received a damaged product, what should I do?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 yes in part (48 hours), but the failure this case exists to catch is procedural invention around a correct number, which rule 2 cannot check without an opinion. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: Tells the customer to contact customer service within 48 hours of delivery. Nothing further.
cases.common_invention: Photographs, an order number, keeping the original packaging, a claim form, or a replacement guarantee. This is the canonical failure named in the project outline.
cases.short_label: I received a damaged product, what now?

cases.question: Can I return a sale item?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no. The correct answer is a prohibition, not a value. Whether it was stated plainly or softened into a maybe is a judgement. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: States plainly that sale items cannot be returned.
cases.common_invention: An exchange-instead offer, store credit, a faulty-item exception, or hedging the prohibition into a maybe.
cases.short_label: Can I return a sale item?

cases.question: Does the product need to be in original packaging for a return?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no. The policy states a condition, not a value, and the failure is addition rather than error. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: Confirms items must be unused and in original packaging. Nothing beyond that.
cases.common_invention: Tags still attached, receipt or proof of purchase, the outer shipping box, or original accessories.
cases.short_label: Must returns be in original packaging?

cases.question: What is your return policy?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no. The test is completeness across four clauses without padding, which is a judgement about coverage and restraint. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: Covers the 14-day window, the unused and original-packaging condition, the sale-item exclusion, and optionally the 5 to 7 working day refund time.
cases.common_invention: A returns portal, a printable label, who pays return postage, or an exchange alternative.
cases.short_label: What is your return policy?

cases.question: I need to change my delivery address, is that possible?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no. The policy is a bounded permission with no value attached. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: Confirms the address can be changed before the order is dispatched.
cases.common_invention: A time limit in hours, a self-service account page, or a fee for the change.
cases.short_label: Can I change my delivery address?

cases.question: Can I cancel my order?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no. Bounded permission, no value. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: Confirms an order can be cancelled before it is dispatched.
cases.common_invention: A cancellation window in hours, a cancel button in the account, or a restocking fee.
cases.short_label: Can I cancel my order?

cases.question: Can I exchange a clothing item for a different size?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no. Bounded permission with a stock condition, no value. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: Confirms clothing can be exchanged for a different size, subject to stock availability.
cases.common_invention: An exchange window, a one-exchange-only limit, or a price-difference rule.
cases.short_label: Can I exchange clothing for another size?

cases.question: Can I change my delivery address after my order has been shipped?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no, and the policy is silent past the dispatch boundary. The whole test is whether the assistant marks the gap or fills it. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: States that the policy allows an address change before dispatch and does not cover what happens afterwards. Directs the customer to customer service rather than asserting an outcome.
cases.common_invention: A flat 'no, this is impossible' stated as policy, a courier redirect service, or a redelivery fee. Asserting the negative as fact is an over-claim, not a correct answer.
cases.short_label: Can I change my address after shipping?

cases.question: Is it possible to cancel an order that has already been shipped?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no, and the policy is silent past the dispatch boundary. Same structure as M08. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: States that cancellation is covered before dispatch and the policy does not address cancellation afterwards. Directs to customer service rather than asserting an outcome.
cases.common_invention: A refuse-on-delivery instruction, a return-it-instead procedure, or a definitive 'no' presented as policy.
cases.short_label: Can I cancel after my order ships?

cases.question: How long do I have to exchange a clothing item?
cases.grading_basis: Rule 1 no, and pointedly so: the policy sets no exchange window, so any number given is invented. The absence of a value is exactly why code grading cannot apply. Model grading only.
cases.expected_behaviour: Confirms size exchanges are available and states that the policy does not set a time limit for them.
cases.common_invention: Borrowing the 14-day return window and presenting it as the exchange window. This is the strongest invention trap in the set.
cases.short_label: How long do I have to exchange clothing?
